name: T-72 (various modernized variants)

cost.display: ~$2.0–2.5M per modernized/refurbished unit (general open-source estimate — most T-72B3s are Soviet-era hulls overhauled, not newly built, so this is directional rather than a confirmed transaction price)

short_role: Main battle tank used for direct-fire support, breakthrough attempts, and defensive strongpoints; the most numerous armor type in the conflict.
characteristics: Composite/ERA (explosive reactive armor) packages on modernized variants
Widely produced and stockpiled — numbers rather than individual sophistication are its main advantage
employment_notes: Increasingly used in small numbers or singly rather than in the massed armored formations classic doctrine assumed, because a tank moving in the open within a reconnaissance drone's radius is a very findable, very killable target for loitering munitions and FPV drones.
contrast_vs_traditional: Cold War-era doctrine expected large armored formations to punch through defensive lines under cover of artillery and air support. Persistent drone reconnaissance over the whole depth of the battlefield has made massed armor movement extremely costly, pushing tanks toward dispersed use, improvised anti-drone cage armor, and much heavier reliance on EW/jamming escort to survive movement near the line.

reactive_behavior.description: On select: short movement, turret traverse, main gun fires.

connections.description: Fuel and ammunition resupply from a near-rear logistics point.
Crew casualties routed into the tactical casevac chain.
Target designation and fire calls relayed via squad-level terminal.
